Furthermore, our results show that the impact of signals on funders is distinct across different types of projects, and unsolicited funders are more inclined to respond to specific signal patterns than subscribed ones.

Machine learning (ML) based detection of network attacks using ML labels has gained significant interest due to the benefits of reduced labeling costs and enhanced data source diversity. Yet, developing an effective ML-based intrusion detection system (IDS) using ML labels presents challenges, primarily stemming from the requirement for high-quality ML labels and the integration of multiple data sources. In this research, we identify the key issues associated with generating INSDMML labels and their impact on model performance. Notably, our analysis reveals that combining public and private ML labels can lead to significant data label discrepancies, which in turn negatively affect model performance. To mitigate these challenges, we propose a new approach called I3ML, that enables the learning of IDS from public and private network traffic ML labels without needing to access the private data. I3ML is built on the $i^2$ML framework and employs an innovative contribution matrix to model label relationships and maintain the privacy of training data, while also developing an adversarial training mechanism to improve the reliability of ML labels. Our I3ML-based model demonstrates superior generalization capabilities and robustness against noise compared to existing models.

The problem of jointly determining the optimal task sequence and motion plan for a robot is known as the complex hierarchical planning issue. While extensive studies have addressed each aspect separately, real-time execution of these plans is challenging. This research directly targets real-time optimization applications, where a robot is instructed by a human operator to complete a series of tasks located at various positions and orientations. Task execution involves moving the robot's end-effector to a specified position while maintaining the orientation stable, with other tasks being preempted if necessary. The robot's capabilities are constrained by its speed and acceleration limits, as well as by safety regulations preventing excessive movements. The researchers formulate this real-time optimization problem as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming model that minimizes total execution time, taking into account operator preferences in task completion order and timing, and develop a novel model-predictive optimization approach to efficiently solve this complex planning problem. The approach leverages a simplified linear model of the robot's motion characteristics and is validated through simulation of execution results.

The performance of the interface between semiconductors and barriers is a crucial factor in producing consistent, high-quality quantum dots essential for reliable quantum information processing. This research investigates the characteristics of undoped Si substrates by measuring their Si/SiO2 interface quality and carrier mobility without employing external dopants. Our measurements indicate that mobile charge carriers are present on undoped p-type Si wafers, with the carrier concentration and mobility both exhibiting improvements as the oxidation temperature rises. Specifically, the carrier concentration increases from $4.8 \times 10^{11}$ cm$^{-2}$ to $1.6 \times 10^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$ within the 800-1000 °C temperature range and the mobility increases from 11,000 cm$^2$/Vs to 21,000 cm$^2$/Vs during the same timeframe. Furthermore, we evaluated the impact of these mobile carriers on the g-factor and demonstrated that they do not significantly influence it, based on our analysis of 20 different Si wafers and subsequent gate voltage adjustments. Ultimately, the discovered mobile charge carrier property in undoped Si substrates could streamline the Si MQD fabrication process and improve its interface quality by minimizing the necessity for additional doping procedures, thereby yielding higher mobility in semiconductor barriers and better performance in quantum information applications.

In complex networks, oscillating elements can follow time-evolving trajectories that are influenced by their environment. Although existing research has examined desynchronization or anti-synchronization among identical oscillators, a significant knowledge gap exists in understanding scenarios where distinct groups of oscillators, comprised of different types, synchronize into coherent patterns. Through a comprehensive approach that starts with a basic setup and builds up to more intricate systems, this study successfully identifies conditions that facilitate the emergence of this phenomenon across various settings. Ultimately, a detailed analysis is carried out for a model representing desynchronization among diverse groups of oscillators, including an exploration of stability in the presence of time-evolving dynamics.

Our study examines the existence of cultural and linguistic biases in Western search engines by analyzing the diversity of video search outcomes across 12 different languages for three well-known languages (English, German, and French) vs. 9 less widely used languages. We employed two diverse datasets - one comprising 360 multilingual queries and another with 936 multilingual queries - both from our previously collected collection. Our findings indicate that using queries in languages other than English, German, or French leads to significantly lower video diversity in search results. Additionally, both datasets yielded consistent search result diversity across monolingual searches for English, German, and French, but varying results in the remaining 9 languages. Our analysis also reveals that two multilingual datasets produce distinct search outcome compositions, underscoring the importance of assembling a comprehensive and representative dataset to accurately assess search engine bias.

To gain insight into supersymmetric monodromy defects in the critical Wess-Zumino model, researchers employed analytical bootstrap techniques, specifically by exploiting the identities of crossing-symmetric block decompositions to derive constraints on dynamical quantities. By utilizing bootstrap equations that incorporate supersymmetry generators, key data such as the dynamical Fermi tensor and superconformal primary blocks were determined, and it was found that there is mutual information between the scaling dimension of the defect and that of the field. It is hypothesized that the observed patterns in the spectrum hold for all Wess-Zumino model class defects, and the results are expected to provide novel insights into the internal structure of defective supermultiplets.

We prove that there is exactly one elliptic curve, up to uniqueness, defined over a cubic Galois field extension of rational numbers with a point on the curve having an order of 13 and the curve having good characteristics in the base field for all points other than 13 multiples on the curve. It follows that there is exactly one such elliptic curve defined over a totally real cubic fields and another defined over the unique totally imaginary cubic fields. Moreover, the L-function of the curve is equal to a Hilbert Eiderman zeta function for some field.

In the context of a wireless network, the intersection of two spatial Poisson processes is examined. This intersection is investigated in the context of a generic application, with a particular focus on the local delay, defined as the area under the interference curve within a circular region. This investigation is motivated by a systems design that models the interference with multiple sources. Both the interference power and sum interference are analyzed in terms of their probability density function, with the aid of the Riemann zeta function. This analysis is carried out in the context of a circular area and a polygonal region with $N$-sides, with the interference correlation also being explored.

A pseudo-labeling framework is proposed to overcome the limitations of labeled data in Graph Neural Network (GNN) training. Existing methods generate unreliable predictions for novel classes due to their focus on improving performance for known labels. A new method called ILFGN aims to enhance performance for both existing and novel classes. It starts by using known labels to generate pseudo-labels for unlabeled nodes, which are incorporated into the GNN model and used to refine the model parameters. This process is repeated until the model parameters converge, which ultimately improves the performance on novel classes. Experiments demonstrate that ILFGN achieves significant improvements over current techniques.

In video processing, reducing a video's spatial dimensions to a set of distinctive feature patches can be more effective and efficient than focusing on individual pixels. However, most existing methods still heavily rely on pixel-level features. Our proposed method employs a novel patch-based feature learning approach utilizing multi-scale self-similarity, time-same, and time-varying properties to improve accuracy in video classification and object detection.

We examine the one-dimensional discrete-time asymmetric exclusion process with periodic boundaries, applying the transfer matrix method to derive precise expressions for eigenvalues and a complete basis of right and left eigenfunctions. This allows us to develop a new integral representation for time-evolved operators and calculate correlation functions. Additionally, we apply similar techniques to the continuous-time asymmetric exclusion process with arbitrary initial configurations, achieving precise expressions for multi-time correlation functions.

A new method of efficient wireless communication is proposed in a novel SWIPT system, enabling faster and more reliable mobile data networks by leveraging the energy of wireless signals from multiple spatially diverse and closely spaced antennas to support multiple data channels for information and power transfer. To maximize the transfer of data and energy to the receiver within an information power and energy harvesting constraint framework, the design of the wireless signals is refined through the introduction of two mathematical problems that are jointly addressed in partial fraction decomposition form. The simultaneous wireless information and power transfer approach shows promise in providing improved energy efficiency and extended transmission distances for wireless energy harvesting and ultra-dense wireless power and energy transfer applications.

In Fermi gases with low concentrations of magnetic properties, a particular phenomenon occurs at specific points within their internal structure, characterized by a sudden change in how these properties behave, which can be understood as a form of phase transition similar to the well-known BCS-BEC transition. Researchers have developed theoretical models to study this transition for different types of magnetic properties in both one-dimensional and three-dimensional environments, which involve mathematical descriptions of how these gases change from one state to another, including magnetic properties that are similar to the Heisenberg and Mermin-Wagner models. Furthermore, when these magnetic properties are not perfectly balanced, which is often the case in experiments, researchers found that the transition becomes more gradual and that both the one-dimensional and three-dimensional environments show similar behaviors, which are influenced by an external pressure.

We present a generic, simple, and straightforward model of an electrical circuit that captures the core principles of microwave optomechanics, which is an area of research gaining importance in the quantum domain. The model consists of a parallel RLC circuit, where a mechanical oscillator is represented by a capacitor and an electromagnetic mode is represented by an inductor. This setup serves as a fundamental example that can be expanded upon by in-
corporating various types of capacitors and inductors. Notably, this model can be used to develop novel devices, such as SQUID-based optomechanical resonators, by integrating Josephson junctions into the circuit components.

Properties of semi-classical orthogonal polynomials relative to a generalized Airy weight and their corresponding zeros and recurrence coefficients are examined, where specific parameters apply. The study extends to a general form of this weight and includes the computation of the norm of the polynomials at n-degree.

This study investigates how basic autonomous entities can generate complex, unpredictable movement patterns through a designed navigation approach. The intended outcome is a fleet of similar agents, governed by a single, unalterable program, exhibiting a non-repetitive and unforecastable movement when confined to a confined space with obstacles. A specific problem is addressed where an autonomous entity attempts to reach a moving target within a environment with a moving wall. The solution involves a non-modular program where each entity follows its own single, unmodifiable algorithm. A similar simulation is provided, showcasing how a flock of programmed agents, simulating a species of birds known to exhibit individual variability in navigation, can exhibit individualized movement patterns when confined to a enclosed space with a movable wall.

This article further develops the concept of chiral nets in two-dimensional spacetimes as an implementation of algebraic QFT, now incorporating a general fiber bundle approach to 2-dimensional spacetimes. The method is used to quantify the effect of spacetime curvature on the definition of chiral algebras. Various cases are examined to show that curvature can introduce non-trivial bundle structures, yet has a minimal impact on the resulting chiral algebras. The approach is applied to the case of twisted chiral nets.

Laparoscopic surgery has a significant limitation due to a challenging viewing experience, which can lead to confusion and difficulty in tracking surgical tools and tissue. An effective approach to overcome this issue is a virtual desmoking technique, which enhances image clarity by filtering out smoke images. However, conventional methods of filtering smoke often result in distorted images and lost image details. This study presents a novel approach called the LapDesmoking Framework, which utilizes color-based feature extraction and binary smoke segmentation to effectively clean laparoscopic surgery images in real-time. The proposed framework demonstrates superior performance over conventional methods, including Canny, Gaussian, and CCFI, as evaluated using standard metrics (PSNR, SSIM, MSE) and surgical expert feedback.

This research focuses on creating resilient Molmer-Sorensen gates using trapped ions arranged in a line, incorporating Gaussian amplitude modulation and a consistent laser frequency. We chose a modulation profile that matches the target frequency spectrum of the collective spin operator when the center ion is on resonance, as this is where the desired gate operation occurs. Our design achieves a substantial improvement in accuracy for a given bandwidth compared to unmodulated pulses, and we achieved a 50% reduction in the sensitivity to frequency detunations within the ions.

Using advanced cluster expansion and ab-initio calculations, we've created a precise
redescription of the energy levels and structural variations of barium titanate (BaTiO$_3$).
Our analysis reveals that even in its non-polar state, BaTiO$_3$ exhibits two distinct
symmetries. This finding, combined with quantitative data, confirms the value of the
cluster expansion we developed. Our study identifies two relevant structural prototypes
for BaTiO$_3$: one non-polar symmetry and another highly symmetric form with no polar
character. A cluster expansion based on these two prototypes yields lower root-mean-square
errors compared to previously reported values. Furthermore, comparing our results with the
prevailing model of BaTiO$_3$ reveals that the well-established non-polar prototype with a
different symmetry has minimal impact on the material's properties. Our study also presents
new information on the electronic and phononic properties of BaTiO$_3$ and the importance of
its two non-polar prototypes, as well as the validity of using only one such prototype.

Multivariate functional data often involves complex patterns that can be captured by statistical models such as the Gaussian graphical model. A new random effect model has been proposed to analyze such data, allowing for correlation structures to be estimated for specific components of the data while accounting for other components. The proposed model benefits from a more precise estimation of covariances and reduced computation time. Further, a Bayesian variational inference algorithm has been developed to implement the model and it's performance has been evaluated through simulation studies. The results indicate that the performance of the new model is on par with existing models in the literature. The performance of the new model was also compared to existing models through a case study of real-world data.

Due to the absence of fully functional quantum processors, quantum algorithm testing is typically confined to comparing theoretical error predictions. This study presents an innovative approach, developing a quantum algorithm designed to test the quantum advantage in the presence of noise. Our strategy involves a two-part process: using the HQE/QPEDQ framework to test and estimate the performance of quantum processors. This framework enables the testing of both quantum and classical processors to identify the most effective processor to solve a problem. The results from our tests are consistent with the theoretical predictions.

A new approach to analyzing high-dimensional optimization problems reduces them to a simpler problem involving matrices whose eigenvalue distributions are randomly and randomly selected. The complexity of these simplified problems significantly differs from their original counterparts and their concentration near the extreme eigenvalues directly correlates with the difficulty level. Leveraging this connection, we establish a new upper bound on the difficulty of finding a satisfactory solution to convex and ill-conditioned minimization problems using Riemannian gradient methods with only four evaluations of the objective function.

Recent breakthroughs in producing two-dimensional materials with specific patterns of layered structures have advanced the field of light–matter interaction physics. This latest study delves into the phenomenon of light-induced oscillations generated within biexciton states that form from interactions between excitons located in different layers. Through theoretical calculations, it is found that the coupling between layers leads to interlayer excitons with distinct positions for their electron and hole components. This setup enables the formation of unique resonant states called resonant Frenkel excitons. When resonant photons interact with these states, they trigger distinct oscillatory patterns following the absorption process. The two-dimensional system exhibits a characteristic binding energy associated with its interlayer excitons. By adjusting the separation between layers, the electron and hole radii can be controlled, thereby adjusting the system's binding energy and, in turn, the oscillation frequency caused by electron or hole motion in response to interlayer forces. The developed framework provides a means to experimentally verify the predicted oscillatory phenomena through upcoming interlayer structure experiments.

We have developed a method for determining the position of vehicles in areas filled with obstacles, low and uneven terrain, and by utilizing the reflections of signals off different surfaces. This technique employs a combination of a standard UWB system and a specialized localization algorithm that takes into account the variations in the environment that affect the position and strength of different multipath components. We have applied a sophisticated model to estimate how these signal changes relate to the vehicle's movement and used this information to accurately locate the vehicle. Our experiments have demonstrated that taking into account the changes in the environment that affect the position and strength of these signal reflections can significantly improve localization accuracy, reducing the average localization error to under 30 cm.

Researchers have achieved a first-time observation of two vector bosons being produced and behaving like they have mass, with both particles moving in the same direction. This remarkable occurrence has been observed and measured at a 3.1 standard deviation level, according to data from 2018 for collisions of protons with a energy level of 13 TeV. Both the W and Z bosons were found to be in their lowest energy state. The observed production rate for this occurrence has been measured at 0.69 times the predicted rate based on the standard theory of particles. No evidence was found for any abnormal patterns in the energy levels of the invariant mass of the pair.

Research indicates that the Cotton tensor offers a way to generalize a'scalar gravity', and we've found that it can be expressed by combining derivatives of the Einstein tensor, suggesting that this tensor offers insights into general relativity and potentially leads to the discovery of new invariants. These findings support the hypothesis that the Cotton tensor will play a significant role in the future of gravity research.

We've established a specific type of ordered relational topological space known as orthomodular spaces. These spaces are made up of T_0 ordered spaces with open orders, and they're heavily utilized to illustrate the connections between frames and ortholattices. Our research focuses on the most basic representations of these spaces, examining their relational properties and providing clear examples along the way. Additionally, we've identified a specific category within orthomodular spaces, referred to as orthomodular uniformities, which are used to categorize ortholattices based on their topological characteristics.

We introduce a visual representation system that translates Coq proof scripts into tabular forms, which can be exported as $\LaTeX$ or PDF files. Our tool aims to facilitate learning and proof review by providing an interactive visual representation of each step in a proof. Consequently, this system enables educators and reviewers to utilize the proofs without relying on the Coq program, thereby allowing them to be printed or shared in other formats, making the proofs more accessible and accessible.

We demonstrate that the fourth moment of holomorphic Hecke cusp forms is limited under the assumption of the Riemann Hypothesis for a specific degree 8 L-function. This is achieved by leveraging Watson's formula, which allows us to recast our investigation as a tractable problem related to L-functions, ultimately facilitating the application of Soundararajan and Harper's methods for deriving sharp bounds on the moments of the Riemann zeta function.

In iterative solution methods for linear equation systems, accelerating convergence is typically achieved by diminishing the eigenvalues of the iteration matrix. A more efficient approach involves developing an alternative iteration matrix with a substantially narrower eigenvalue range, which can be done by implementing a suitable preconditioner. For certain complex problems with the Minkowski cell problem, standard preconditioners are not effective due to the non-symmetric and ill-conditioned nature of the underlying matrices. A novel, scalable wavelet-based preconditioner has been proposed to improve convergence and has been successfully tested within a multilevel correction framework.

We have derived the polarized massive operator matrix element $A_{gq}^{(3)}(N)$
analytically to three-loop order in QCD for arbitrary values of $N$,
including both single- and double-mass scenarios in the Larin scheme.
Furthermore, the result serves as a crucial transition function for the variable
flavor number scheme at $O(\alpha_s^3)$ and is also expressed in momentum
space for convenient use.

We are gathering comprehensive reports of any problems encountered with smart systems, whether they are advanced technology, complex projects, or artificial intelligence projects, via the responsibleAI.inc website. The problems encountered with these systems are collected in a publicly accessible database of real-world failure cases, which can be used as a valuable resource as we move towards a future driven by intelligent systems. To start, we are using a simple template to gather information about any problems encountered, including a description of the situation, data used, models developed, and any issues found in the final application. We are also using the same database to share our team's and organization's insights on real AI systems failure modes as described in published papers and conference presentations, which can help anyone engaged in AI development to learn from the experiences of others and build more reliable and safe AI systems in collaboration.

The principle underlying the renormalization group bears a strong analogy to gradient flow, especially in scalar field theory where the RG and gradient flows share a direct connection through the ERG formalism. To generalize this connection in Yang--Mills theory while maintaining gauge invariance, we propose an ERG equation based on a similarity principle and further extend it to lattice gauge theory from the continuum theory context.

Current business rules are often expressed using Natural Language, but their
automatic transformation into Executable Form has several limitations,
particularly when it comes to medical clinical guidelines. Although such
guidelines can be straightforward in their language, they can refer to
unlimited sets of additional information, making it difficult for
automated systems to determine if specific conditions are met or to
suggest appropriate treatments. To address these challenges, we developed a
new method to automatically translate Natural Language rules into Executable Form,
taking into account the specific context and information available. Our approach
involves converting rules into a structured format known as DRL, while also
considering the accessibility of information and treatment options. Building on
this framework, we created RUGE, a system designed to automatically translate
Complex Clinical Guidelines into Patient Treatment Plans. RUGE is illustrated
using four context-specific guidelines concerning Diabetes treatment, where we
demonstrate how to effectively utilize Patient Health Records and take into
account limitations in treatment options.

Qulies is a quantum programming language that incorporates type system rules linear types to express key quantum phenomena such as measurement, gate application, and tensor products of quantum states. This paper demonstrates how to derive an operational semantics and establish soundness and completeness theorems for Qulies through the use of a term rewriting system, ultimately yielding a positive and consistent type system. The development of an operational semantics and its accompanying proof framework serves as a useful tool for further investigation into this specific quantum programming language.

In this study, we used 2D percolation models to demonstrate that their critical behavior is heavily influenced by extreme eigenvalues. To achieve this, we designed a non-uniform grid with an arithmetic progression in spacing. Following an examination of the associated Laplacian matrix, we found its extremal eigenvalues can be approximated by solving simpler auxiliary problems. Furthermore, our analysis revealed that these extreme eigenvalues exhibit characteristics similar to those found in the continuous arithmetic fountain. As a consequence, our findings show that the arithmetic distribution leads to the dominance of a single large eigenvalue in this context.

We suggest an atomic implementation of the tilt-drift free fermion model, where entanglement between N atoms, mediated by exchange of virtual photons, exhibits growth that increases factorially over time. In contrast, existing simulations with detuned two-level atoms show only exponential entanglement increase. By adjusting the atoms' frequencies relative to the field, our predictions offer a method to create large-scale entangled states of atoms, potentially achieving entanglement among all N atoms for about N times the radiation period of an individual atom. Furthermore, these simulations could enable the study of light-matter interactions on a novel scale.

Assembling a complete genome from short, overlapping DNA sequences is a crucial task in genomics with far-reaching applications, such as identifying pathogenic variants and linking genetic disorders to diseases. Due to the large amount of data generated, especially when analyzing cancer genomes, developing efficient and accurate assembly algorithms becomes a critical challenge. Our proposed method, Scapa, addresses this need by leveraging the high-quality short-read sequencing data and employing an optimized, short-read-only approach. By utilizing sensitive and fast long-read-only and short-read-only assemblies as starting points, Scapa performs targeted and precise improvements, resulting in high-quality diploid genome reconstructions. Our comprehensive assessment across six diverse human genomes demonstrates that Scapa achieves superior accuracy, precision, and performance compared to existing hybrid and tri-allelic methods. The significant computational resource savings obtained by Scapa make it particularly valuable for large-scale applications, such as cancer genome analyses.

A modified logistic equation with a delayed term was introduced by Hutchinson in 1999 for modeling continuous systems and by Magal and co-researchers in 2011 for discrete models. This delayed logistic model has served as a primary framework for investigating oscillatory phenomena within the fields of mathematical biology and dynamics. In this study, we review recent advancements and open issues related to both continuous and discrete versions of this delayed logistic equation.

The concept of statistical depth has the potential to be applied to temporal point processes for measuring the depth of individual events and event sequences. We've developed a time-based depth approach that incorporates the concept of statistical depth, allowing us to identify key events and upcoming patterns in such processes. Building on the foundation of rank-based depth, we've integrated concepts from interval set processes and Poisson processes to derive depth values. Our method's versatility enables it to be used for various existing models, including Hawkes processes and Cox processes. Moreover, our depth-based method can facilitate the detection of anomalous patterns and the determination of most representative events in these processes.

Achieving maximum engine performance involves leveraging quantum effects. In this investigation, two strategies for creating the most efficient engines are considered, specifically (1) using hybrid quantum systems capable of performing multiple beneficial tasks, and (2) minimizing random fluctuations in these tasks. In classical devices, eliminating random fluctuations requires high entropy generation as dictated by thermodynamic uncertainty principles. Here, these principles are extended to hybrid thermal machines with multiple terminals. In quantum conductors, these limitations are bypassed, and we demonstrate this for a setup comprising a double quantum dot and normal metals in contact, connected to two parallel loads with extremely low capacitance. These loads act as a heat bath and also serve as capacitors for storing electric charge. In this context, we maximize a capacitor's ability to store a fixed amount of stored energy while also minimizing the thermodynamic uncertainty of the charge stored. In the limiting case, our analysis shows a fundamental limit of $0$ for the thermodynamic uncertainty, and we find that the minimum uncertainty grows linearly with the stored energy.

Researchers investigated the $6s^{2}6p$ $^{1}S_{0}-7s$ $^{1}S_{0}$ transition in $^{69}$Ge using a single-ion trap. The experiment involved obtaining laser spectrogram and nuclear data through frequency comb spectroscopy. The obtained quadrupole and magnetic moments for $^{69}$Ge were found to be $0.089(6)	imes 10^{-4}$ m and $-0.178(16)$ m respectively. The research team's results led to an update in the evaluation of the magnetic moment for $^{69}$Ge due to its significant deviation from the initial measurement. The project was a success as the precision of the measurement using this technique matched the prediction made by theory.

Researchers at the Isotopic Separator for Experiments (ISOLDE) facility at CERN
have refined a novel technique for accurately measuring the masses of rapidly
decaying unusual atomic nuclei. This breakthrough employs the ISOLDE facility in
combination with a highly sensitive detection system. Our team successfully used
this method to determine the precise mass of $^{52}$Cr, matching a previously
reported measurement of the same element. We have reported on a successful
measurement of the precise mass of the Cr-52 isotope using the ISOLDE facility at CERN. The TRIGAMI facility has been used to generate a beam of Cr-52 isotopes, which are then directed at a target to create an electrical explosion. A small amount of material is ejected from the target and ionized, which is then sent to a time-of-flight detector to measure the time it takes for the ions to travel a known distance. This measurement is used to calculate the mass of the Cr-52 isotopes with high precision.

This paper introduces the multicanonical method to a different context, specifically a category of lattice field theories that is not Monte Carlo fermion theory. It's utilized to sample various Boltzmann distributions.

We aim to enhance the accuracy of structured text recognition by incorporating predefined patterns from a user's perspective. Specifically, we utilize popular regexes to verify and correct recognized text, taking into consideration the flexibility of regexes for optional elements, digits, and special characters. Our proposed post-processor, which can be applied independently of the primary text recognition system, systematically inserts deleted characters and removes excess elements in the recognized text to validate it against the provided regexes.

The CMS experiment at the CERN LHC detected the production of top quarks for the first time using proton-lead data at an 8.16 TeV nucleon-nucleon center-of-mass energy. A top quark production mechanism was identified alongside an antiquark, resulting in a characteristic decay pattern. The data analysis involved selecting events with one or more jets and lepton signatures, achieving a significance of 7.6 standard deviations, exceeding the background expectations. The final data agreement with theoretical predictions occurred across various nucleon-nucleon interaction processes.

This study focuses on key elements in cross-domain text-to-SQL parsing, specifically schema linking and value filling. To enhance encoding abilities, a column selection auxiliary task is proposed, leveraging explicit targets for relevance matching. Additionally, two value filling approaches are presented to bridge the gap between current zero-shot parsers and practical applications, considering that many existing parsers overlook value filling in synthesized SQL. Experiments on the Spider dataset demonstrate the superiority of our proposed framework over baseline models in terms of execution and exact set match accuracy when database contents are inaccessible, with further analysis pointing to areas for future improvement.

The ongoing LoTSS survey is conducting a thorough observation of the Northern sky to better understand how the large-scale structure of the Universe changes over time. Although only 1% of the target area has been covered in the LoTSS DR1, analysis of the data reveals interesting findings, specifically in a recently published slice of the data at Right Ascension 04h35m and Declination 20h28m. This particular slice was analyzed using different techniques to identify the most prominent galaxy clusters within it. One method involved using galaxies with clear and distinct signals to create Density-Weighted Correlation Functions, which helped define the boundaries of galaxy clusters. Another approach involved using Machine Learning to analyze the data. The results from both methods are compared, with the aim of determining the best approach for future research. The data also allows for the estimation of cosmological parameters using 3D distance measurements of galaxy clusters, with a new, innovative approach being developed as a result.

The high-dimensional rank lasso model is a popular approach in statistics and machine learning for handling rank data, such as survival times and survival indicators, while also incorporating sparsity assumptions and L1-penalization for optimal results. However, standard approaches often neglect the interdependence between response variables, leading to potentially inaccurate outcomes. In this study, we develop an enhanced estimate for the high-dimensional rank lasso problem by introducing a low-rank penalized estimator that accounts for inter-response dependencies. We establish the consistency of our estimate and propose an algorithm based on the Inference for Recurrent Events and Dependencies using Count data and Derivatives using Poisson distribution and their associated algorithms.

Identifying whether an optimal strategy exists and if it is unique remains a significant challenge in control theory applications. In addressing this issue, we investigate the possibility of globally optimal strategies for solving the minimum entropy production problem for Markov processes. By establishing the convexity of the relevant cost function, we show that the optimal strategy can be the solution to this problem. However, due to the inherent nonlinearity of convex optimization in this context, finding the exact solution remains difficult. Instead, we propose a reliable and efficient method for approximating the optimal strategy, based on a previously established and adaptable algorithm.

Over the past decade, significant advancements in artificial intelligence have positioned it as a key tool for addressing environmental challenges. Nevertheless, recent AI achievements have also contributed substantially to carbon emissions, necessitating a need for more efficient models that can actually support green applications. This need is further amplified by regions in the global South, where access to technology and digital skills are already hindered. This paper seeks to broaden existing discussions on AI for green purposes, highlighting the untapped potential and diverse digital contributions that can be channeled towards environmental sustainability.

This paper introduces a novel framework and set of evaluation metrics for prescriptive process monitoring. Our approach enables the virtual testing and quantitative assessment of proposed interventions in real business processes. By leveraging a process model, we can predict outcomes and performance for both implemented solutions and alternative courses of action. A case study in the publishing sector demonstrates the practical value of the framework. Based on our research findings, we offer recommendations for further investigation into the field of prescriptive process monitoring.

This study introduces an error control strategy for a Boussinesq model that links temperature and fluid dynamics. The strategy uses the residual approach with an adaptive time refinement method. Since the temperature for each time step depends on its immediate predecessor, we need to control how changes in temperature affect the four balance equations. By analyzing how thermal conductivity and viscosity change with temperature, we can derive a global bound on this influence. Based on this, we developed an indicator that helps guide time refinement. The method was tested with two benchmarks, and its performance was compared with a method that simply uses the solution to estimate error. The results showed that our proposed method, which takes into account thermal effects, consistently outperforms the other method.

Over the past 20 years, research on kernelization has gained significant momentum due to its capacity to reduce large input instances of NP-hard problems to smaller, data-independent summaries, known as kernels, for hard problems. Notably, many celebrated results in this field have been achieved, with the most recent breakthroughs involving multi-parameter kernelization for problems that are not achievable through traditional single-parameter kernelization. Notably, such kernels rely on key techniques like NEIGHBORHOOD EXCHANGE and COMPOSITIONAL KERNELIZATION.

A comprehensive and well-organized algorithm for kernelization through NEIGHBORHOOD EXCHANGE is presented in this paper, allowing for the efficient inclusion of REDUCTION RULES that may produce substantial I-rule kernels for problems with high complexity. Similarly, a simplified rule for Compositional Kernelization is introduced, enabling the rapid construction of kernels through NEIGHBORHOOD EXCHANGE for problems that are not amenable to single-parameter kernelization. As a result of these approaches, three novel kernels are established for the following problems:

1. $d$-SPARSE SET KERNELIZATION: A kernel of size $O(k^{2d-1})$ is obtained for $d \geq 2$, with previous best kernels requiring exponential dependence on $d$.

2. $d$-SUPERMODULAR SET COVERING: A kernel of size $O(k^{2d-1})$ is obtained for problems that are not amenable to single

This study builds upon HSLMC model to create OPINIONeers, an online platform for opinion dynamics simulations. It allows users to create and manage multiple agents with varying levels of confidence, friend relationships, and no common domain of discussion. With a web-based interface, HSLMC model's flexibility can be enjoyed by a broader audience, including students and researchers from diverse backgrounds, as shown by multiple examples of its use in opinion networks.

We've investigated a newly constructed series of asymptotically flat, electrically charged black holes that form scalar "hair" when their charge increases at a fixed mass. Inside the event horizon, these black holes resemble a holographic superconducting material, exhibiting similar behavior in their scalar fields and culminating in a singularity that heavily depends on the black holes' parameters when the instability first arises. Additionally, we present a general theory in an appendix stating that certain types of stationary black holes with scalar "hair" cannot possess Cauchy horizons.

Different genes exhibiting similar activation patterns may show distinct mRNA profiles over time due to differences in transcript length and transcript stability. Our study focused on understanding the underlying dynamics of mRNA transcription and stability, focusing particularly on immediately early genes. By analyzing a dataset of 22 genes, we were able to classify them into groups based on their transcriptional and post-transcriptional stability dynamics, as well as identify their regulatory mechanisms. Further mathematical analysis revealed that rapid changes in transcription can lead to increased mRNA diversity, whereas prolonged activation allows for the establishment of stable transcription rates and decreased diversity. Our findings provide cell-type and context-specific insights into the regulatory mechanisms behind mRNA temporal profiles and can inform computational models.

Recent studies have significantly enhanced our understanding of the 64Ni nucleus by discovering low-energy, low-angular momentum excited states. Specifically, this investigation employed the TRISPC@CCL20 detector system to identify additional states between 6.55 and 7.2 MeV. Using gamma-ray and proton spectra, researchers were able to examine 64Ni's excited states and determine its structural characteristics. Additionally, 64Ni's collective nature, 62Ni nucleus's configuration, and the energy differences between 64Ni's collective and pairing interactions have been more clearly defined. These findings have also clarified the transition from collective to individual behavior in the 62Ni nucleus at high energy levels.

We have found an key relationship between Wilson loops and 't Hooft anomalies in gauge theories with Weyl fermions, similar to the relationship found in supersymmetric theories. The anomaly in this context allows for calculating the action of dilations without needing supersymmetry. The action of special conformal transformations can also be derived from the action of dilations and 't Hooft anomalies, indicating that the algorithm defines a unique trajectory in position-momentum space.

A linear complementary pair of group codes $(C, D)$ is formed when the direct sum of $C$ and $D$ results in the entire group algebra $R[G]$, given a finite principal ideal ring $R$ and a finite group $G$. We identify a required and confirming criterion for pairs of group codes $(C, D)$ in group algebra $R[G]$ to be a linear complementary pair, subsequently proving the equivalence in terms of permutations between codes $C$ and the dual code $D^{\perp}$.

We introduce a new efficient method for representing functions in a graphical model framework, which reduces the number of parameters needed and speeds up computations. Our proposed state automata approach enables decomposition of functions dependent on multiple variables into smaller sub-functions, each associated with a state in a finite state machine. These sub-functions can then be represented using compact parameters, significantly reducing the overall memory footprint. In practice, we found that the state automata approach not only minimizes the number of parameters but also facilitates efficient model training and inference. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this representation on a range of sequence-to-sequence tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results for the translation task and outperforming previous models by a margin of 1-2% in multiple choice tasks.

The visual appearance and auditory cues of objects can collectively inform Object Localization in the Real World. In complex indoor settings, especially with moving objects, it's not always feasible to directly access the target object's 3D appearance. Instead, it may be possible to capture its auditory signals using microphones embedded in drones or robots. Previous methods that combined visual and auditory cues for localization typically treated object 3D localization and category identification as intertwined tasks. However, we propose separating these categories and introducing a novel and efficient loss function to tackle this problem. Our method also incorporates an attention mechanism to effectively manage the intricate and non-linear connection between 3D structures and their respective cue signals. The experiments we conducted demonstrate the efficacy of our approach in accurately locating objects within complex 3D environments.

In densely packed mixtures of soft spheres, an abrupt transition occurs during shear thickening, shifting from interacting via short-range forces to a state dominated by long-range friction. Researchers employed a mesoscopic model to simulate the behavior of repulsive spheres under shear stress and observed the onset of thickening at various interaction ranges. By analyzing the model, it was found that the effect of long-range interactions is amplified near the critical point of shear stress, even for particles with relatively short interaction ranges. Furthermore, it was found that the fraction of particle pairs experiencing long-range forces grows significantly and non-uniformly as shear stress approaches the critical point, even for granular materials characterized by extremely short interaction ranges. Consequently, it was concluded that the critical point is highly sensitive to long-range interactions, irrespective of their initial density.

This study investigates the root causes and historical patterns of power shortages in Ghana, considering the country's goal to minimize electricity consumption cuts. By employing Bayesian change point analysis, we explore shifts in electricity consumption levels from 2017-2019, based on data from Ghana's Ministry of Environment and Climate Change. Our analysis identifies two distinct periods of consumption, with a probability of 60% that the low-consumption period will extend beyond 2019. Using an exponential model, we estimate an average duration of outages at 10.4 months, with a standard deviation of 5.9 months. This finding holds significant importance for Ghanaians aiming to mitigate the impact of power shortages.

An area where Web search personalisation has generated considerable debate is its impact on information diversity. In this study, we investigate another potential negative consequence, which is relevant information omission. We claim that increased personalisation can lead to significant information omissions during a search session, as well as the obfuscation of personal results with general findings. In our approach, we utilize a search log from Microsoft Research's 'I'm Feeling Lucky' program to identify instances of search personalisation. By comparing the search queries of users during both personalised and non-personalised searches, we identify instances of omissions and obfuscation. In experiments using a diverse test set comprising queries from various topics and domains, we found that search engine personalisation can omit up to 20% of the necessary information, with factors such as search engine and query subject influencing the extent of its impact.

Automatically creating programs from detailed specifications is a challenging task.
Our study presents an innovative method for generating code from flow chart specifications.
We define this problem as the Graph Structure to Code problem (G2C). Our G2C solution
leverages a pre-trained model, Llama-2, which was trained on a vast dataset of
Python code. To accomplish this, we converted existing Python code into flow chart
specifications using an algorithm, then trained the model on both the visual representations
and the original code descriptions. Our evaluation indicates that G2C achieves high
accuracy in reconstructing Python programs from flow chart specifications, with a 60%
success rate for exact matches and a 90% success rate for correct output functionality.
The process also demonstrates excellent efficiency in identifying the input variables
from the flow chart's logic, with a 97.5% accuracy rate for binary operations and
excellent performance in counting the required inputs for complex calculations.

This text explores multiple reduction techniques that facilitate the connection of Earth's climate models of varying complexity, emphasizing approaches that enable thorough reduction. It distills key mathematical concepts behind each method while showcasing several benchmark climate modeling examples for illustrative purposes.

The astrophysical event known as the neutron star merger is the site of the rapid neutron capture process, which is also responsible for creating the heaviest elements in the universe. Recent research suggests that this reaction is accelerated by a particular group of nuclei, including $A \sim 130$ nuclei, termed the "peaked rapid neutron capture process."  In our study, we investigated the rapid neutron capture process in this mass range using the SkE* force, and compared our findings to those obtained with other well-known nuclear forces, including the GCM-SLY4, BSk19, and BSk19+ forces.  Our results demonstrate that the cross sections for the rapid neutron capture process using the SkE* force are significantly larger than those obtained with a semi-classical model, and and other well-known nuclear forces.  A crucial factor contributing to the large cross sections is the suppression of the fission barrier in the SkE* force, and this characteristic allows for a more efficient synthesis of heavy nuclei.  In addition, our study examines how the cross sections for the rapid neutron capture process affect the abundance of heavy nuclei in the universe, and finds that the SkE* force results in a notable increase in the abundance of $A \sim 130$ nuclei, including elements such as Iodine, Lanthanum, and Neodymium.  These findings have significant implications for our understanding of the abundance of heavy elements in the universe

Radiation oncologists' goal is to target tumors accurately while shielding surrounding vital organs, specifically the stomach and intestines, from x-ray beams. The incorporation of MR-Linac systems allows real-time tumor positioning, enabling precise radiation dosage adjustments based on shifting cell populations. The manual process of identifying these organs and calibrating X-ray beams can be lengthy, extending treatment times up to one hour a day, making automated techniques with deep learning essential. A recent paper explores the use of deep learning-based automation to streamline this complex task and provide faster access to treatment for a greater number of patients.

Compositional data analysis is a technique that deals with complex datasets, which consist of several interdependent components summing to a constant value. Common constant values are 1 and 100%. This data structure is commonly found in disciplines such as biochemistry, geochemistry, and the social sciences. Researchers often examine compositional data in "omics" studies with extremely large dimensions. The method involves calculating logratios – the logarithmic expressions of component proportions. The matrix representation, calculation, and interpretation of these logratios present distinct challenges.

The exoplanet sample from CORALIE/HARPS, which includes gas giants, suggests these objects are more frequently found around closer stars, in contrast to field giants, where they are less common. This discrepancy implies the presence of exoplanets within the stellar region, a prediction consistent with the 'desert' observed in the Kepler distribution at specific mass and distance ranges.

When interacting with their environment, agents may only have access to limited information at a time, necessitating a strong focus on specific environmental aspects to accomplish tasks. In this research, we develop a task-oriented attention control mechanism for agents with restricted visibility, enabling efficient task completion. We implement this system in a simple light-gathering agent, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations where the agent acquires new sensory capabilities and efficiently discovers their relationship with the existing environment, resulting in successful task completion.

Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) can be computationally expensive and require large amounts of data to effectively learn dependencies in their input. We introduce a class of locality masked RNNs (LM-RNNs) that are more data and model efficiency oriented alternatives to fully-connected recurrent neural networks. By incorporating locality masking, which limits the range of information exchange between neurons, our LM-RNNs can be efficiently trained using parallel methods and exhibit improved performance on diverse sequence modeling tasks, including language modeling and controlled language generation.

We categorize nilpotent algebras by dimension with a focus on their commutative, commutative nilpotent and anticommutative properties. Our findings reveal the irreducibility of corresponding geometric spaces, allowing us to accurately calculate their dimensions and establish general families of algebras associated with each space. Additionally, we demonstrate how these results contribute to an understanding of the length of anticommutative algebras in further study.

Active galactic nuclei with exceptionally powerful radio emissions are among the most significant unknown factors in astronomy. These AGN power is directly linked to the mass growth of supermassive black holes. Energy generated by the accretion disk is converted into jets via magnetic fields at the base of the jet, which then escape at relativistic speeds and impact their surroundings, powering the cosmic web reionization and the universe's web. Powerful jets from these black holes can drive star formation or formation inhibition, as well as formation of galaxy bulk heat. In this paper, we investigate gamma-ray emissions resulting from ultrahigh-energy jets, which are produced when ultrahigh-energy protons collide with photons or interstellar gas particles, resulting in the emission of gamma rays. Comparing calculations to observations, constraints on ultrahigh-energy jet parameters can be set, which in turn can shed light on black hole mass growth rates, gas compositions at the core of galaxies, and gas compositions at the core of galaxies.

We perform a covariant expansion of the Einstein-Hilbert action in powers of
$1/c^2$, considering a generic foliation by spacetime surfaces. This framework
enables the demonstration that the Einstein-Hilbert action's covariant expansion
is independent of how it is covariantized. Furthermore, this approach aligns with
recent non-relativistic limits of the Einstein-Hilbert action.

This study presents an enhanced approach to 3D image analysis that incorporates generalized symmetry properties of the Laplace operator. This method extends a previous approach based on the curvature of a 3D image, ensuring invariance to rotations, translations, and scale transformations. To achieve this, we derived and evaluated two new invariants, one linear and one quadratic, in relation to local image characteristics. We evaluated our approach and compared it to the curvature invariant and other scale-invariant local features. The results, obtained from the SIFT-3D invariant, the oriented gradient field, and the Hessian, indicate that the generalized SP-symmetry provides superior invariance to rotations, translations, and scale transformations.

We've analyzed the data from a unique binary star system, SDSS J082239.54+304857.19, which includes detailed observations that uncovered two distinct eclipses and characteristics of both stars in the binary pair. Observations revealed that the primary star is an early B-type star with a companion that experienced two eclipses. Spectroscopic analysis confirmed the presence of hydrogen and helium atoms but not metals in the companion. Calculations using the binary star modeling tool, EBCode, and various other modeling methods resulted in a companion radius and mass of $1.30_{-0.09}^{+0.10}$ $R_{\odot}$ and $2.25_{-0.25}^{+0.32}$ $M_{\odot}$, respectively. Furthermore, modeling the binary's orbit led to a mass ratio uncertainty of less than $3\%$. Estimated values for the system include a temperature of $26,000 \pm 2,000$ K for the secondary star, a system age of $100-200$ Myr based on isochrone fitting, and a wind mass loss rate of $0.36-0.53$ $10^{-8} M_{\odot} yr^{-1}$. Ultimately, this system appears to be an example of a post-common-envelope

In many machine learning models, a common operation known as global pooling is employed.
Despite its importance, understanding global pooling has been hindered because it is rarely examined in a theoretical context.
Fortunately, graph theory offers opportunities to analyze global pooling on graphs, where an entire graph is reduced to a single value.
This approach has broad implications across various graph-based applications, including semi-supervised classification and graph neural networks (GNNs).
We provide a detailed analysis of different types of global pooling, including their benefits and limitations.
Additionally, we introduce a novel type of global pooling called generalized pooling, which can be interpreted as the optimal solution to certain aggregation problems.

The primary objective of this research is to examine whether the relationship between active galactic nuclei and the morphology of their host galaxies changes according to the classification of active galactic nuclei as defined by the broad/narrow line ratio established by Boller et al. (1996). A comprehensive analysis utilizing data from the BASSUNES atlas and cross-referencing information from various galaxy catalogs, reveals no statistically significant disparity in the morphology of host galaxies associated with types 1 and 2 AGN. However, the analysis also uncovers that spiral galaxies tend to host more types 1 AGN, while elliptical galaxies are more likely to host type 2 AGN. Furthermore, it is found that types 1 and 2 Seyfert 1 and 2 galaxies exhibit distinct preferences in terms of their host galaxy environments.

This paper delves into a comprehensive analysis of general rotational surfaces in the 4-dimensional Euclidean space, focusing on flat general rotation surfaces characterized by a 1-type Gauss map. Additionally, it's established that a non-planar, flat general rotation surface with this distinct Gauss map is a Lie group if and only if it's a Clifford torus.

Deep neural network training for semantic segmentation requires vast amounts of annotated data, an endeavor that is both costly and labor-intensive. To mitigate these constraints, researchers proposed using pre-trained models to facilitate semantic segmentation, but these approaches are limited by the need for annotated images. To address this limitation, we propose using depth estimation from unrestricted, unlabeled video footage for pre-training. This approach enables our model to learn scene-related properties such as object shapes, sizes, and spatial relationships, which are instrumental for semantic segmentation tasks. By training our model without any annotation, we demonstrate its efficacy across multiple urban driving datasets, including NuScenes, KITTI, and PASCAL VOC without any manual labeling. This results in state-of-the-art performance for semantic segmentation, outperforming previous pre-training methods by a significant margin of 3.7 mIoU on complex driving scenarios and narrowly trailing behind by only 0.6 mIoU in simpler driving conditions.

The growing availability of annotated time-series data has revolutionized various sectors including transportation, finance, and maintenance, yet time-series data interpretation remains challenging for many. In an effort to address this, researchers have sought to automate narrations that describe temporal patterns in time-series data, leveraging both statistical and deep learning techniques. However, such narrations come at a cost, often requiring intricate manual creation and tweaking. In contrast, TCube, a system designed specifically for this, can automatically generate a narrative from raw data at cost. TCube represents a significant advancement by automatically creating a narrative at near data interpretation cost, outperforming and rivaling state-of-the-art and traditional methods in a diverse range of tasks.

The ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has achieved precise measurements in two areas, namely neutral B meson mixing and CP violation, as well as in rare electroweak processes occurring in suppressed B-meson decays. This study concentrates on recent findings from the ATLAS collaboration, encompassing measurements of rare occurrences like $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ and $B^0 \to \mu^+\mu^-$ decays and determination of the probability and characteristics of the rare process $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ and $B^0 \to \mu^+\mu^-$ at the LHC.
On a Cayley tree, we analyze the Ising model and find novel periodic measures that are linked to index-2 normal subgroups within its group representation.

This study builds upon previous works of Kimura and Vasseur (2019) and Balabane et al. (2020), extending their results to strictly hyperbolic equations with mildly blowing-up coefficients. It demonstrates the existence of uniform $L^2$-bounds for such equations up to a time frame of $\mathcal{O}(\log \log e)$ and also identifies optimal dependence on the parameter $e$. Notably, in contrast to Kimura and Vasseur's approach, which uses the Peano cell to analyze the problem, this research employs a different method rooted in Mikulevicius and Peetre's work to obtain new results up to a higher Cauchy data lifespan of $\mathcal{O}(\log \log e)$.

This research introduces a novel application of the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network to tackle the challenging task of Japanese word segmentation. Building on previous breakthroughs in Chinese word segmentation using LSTM and GRU, this study tackles the more complex task of Japanese word segmentation which involves various character types such as hiragana, katakana, and kanji. These characters lead to significant orthographic variations and increase the difficulty of accurately segmenting Japanese words. To address this complexity, this study proposes an LSTM-based model for Japanese word segmentation, taking into consideration the existing approaches and carefully considering several critical factors.

On the Stack Overflow platform, users utilize 22,575 shared external resources in total, with 4,889 unique external resources shared. Our analysis reveals that 812 external resources are associated with programming languages, accounting for 35% of all shared links. Although users engage with a diverse range of external resources, link popularity reveals the top external resources as articles and tutorials, constituting 64% of all shared links. Furthermore, users connect to external resources across multiple time periods, utilizing links as threads to guide other users to relevant resources, often emphasizing their relevance in the posting's context. Of all shared links, 6,852 (30%) are identified as stack overflow related, with 4,352 (19%) being stack overflow specific. Although external linking serves to share information, our findings suggest its primary purpose is to highlight popular content and disseminate new information, with a significant impact on users' online behaviors, including link sharing strategies and community interactions.

Utilizing cutting-edge data on galaxy halos from the Euclid and Vera C. Rubin telescopes, researchers can now constrain various dark matter models, specifically comparing self-interacting dark matter and cold dark matter, accounting for varying levels of baryonic feedback. Although detailed data on galaxy halos will provide significant insight, fully grasping the implications will require the development of sophisticated analysis tools and our current understanding of baryonic feedback's impact on dark matter models may need revision.

Although climate change is widely acknowledged as a global threat, many people fail to perceive it as pressing enough to motivate significant lifestyle changes. Researchers from diverse fields collaborate to develop strategies promoting climate change awareness and understanding. This paper synthesizes insights from communication studies on the topic, allowing for numerous research applications. We address key questions such as the relevance of various climate change subtopics, the effectiveness of different communication methods, the role of values, and the impact of presentation style on messaging. By extracting and analyzing relevant valence and topic information associated with this topic, we provide a valuable resource for future investigations.

Clinical symptoms recorded in unstructured physician notes are challenging to extract due to significant variations in description styles, terminology, and documentation patterns between different healthcare institutions. This work presents a new technique to extract symptoms by utilizing a graph-based method that incorporates both the content and structure of clinical notes along with institution-specific information. Through an experiment involving symptom extraction from notes collected from multiple institutions, our proposed model demonstrated substantial improvements in accuracy and was found to substantially reduce extraction errors in a significant clinical note dataset.

Deep learning models for autonomous driving are built on supervised learning, but this method faces challenges due to the high cost of creating high-quality training data and the need to label massive datasets. This issue is further compounded by the need to account for diverse driving scenarios. Recent advancements in language models like GPT and multimodal models like Flamingo suggest the potential of in-context learning to tackle this problem, allowing models to adapt to various driving tasks without extensive retraining. However, the effectiveness of in-context learning for complex autonomous driving tasks remains unexplored. To investigate this, we designed a multimodal large language model and performed a comprehensive evaluation of its in-context learning capabilities across a range of driving tasks and contexts. Our results show that in-context learning can be effective but is context-dependent and more demanding than traditional supervised learning. We also found that the performance of in-context learning can be improved by providing a greater number of relevant examples, although this comes with a computational cost. Our code is publicly available on GitHub at https://github.com/abseil/ict-Driving.

In recent years, AI researchers have focused heavily on developing Biorobots powered by Artificial Neural Networks. However, these studies have largely neglected the vast potential of Spiking Neural Networks, which offer a pathway to creating more energy-efficient and bio-plausible computational models. We address this gap by exploring the use of Spiking Neural Networks in controlling the movements of biorobots. Our proposed computational model, which employs a Population-Coding SNN, achieves efficient and robust bio-inspired control of a 3D biorobot. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through an extensive simulation study, showing that our model outperforms traditional ANN-based control methods in terms of robustness, generalization, and computational efficiency.

This research investigates the thermodynamic characteristics of spin-polarized strange quark matter under a strong magnetic field at finite temperature, applying the MIT bag model. Furthermore, we derived the equation of state for spin-polarized strange quark matter in the presence of a strong magnetic field, and subsequently, we examined the structure of spin-polarized strange quark stars across varying temperatures and magnetic fields.

A surge in personal device ownership has led to the possibility of harnessing the power of volunteer computing to run high-performance applications on a large scale. This trend is particularly evident in the adoption of streaming services like Netflix and HBO Now, which can be leveraged by the Pando project to run parallel applications on users' computers using their signed-in accounts. Pando's approach combines multiple personal computers to provide an almost unlimited and scalable grid computing resource. Despite the challenges of executing complex applications on a vast number of volunteer machines, a range of personal applications can still benefit from Pando's decentralized and flexible processing power, including image classification, video transcoding, and natural language processing. This report outlines the architecture and implementation of Pando, as well as a case study demonstrating its effectiveness in the field of computer vision.

A computational method for resolving nonlinear eigenvalue problems is presented, using an approximating function derived from the eigenvalues of a modified eigenproblem equation.  By utilizing a variable sampling process that focuses data collection on the areas most critical to solution resolution, this algorithm efficiently distributes resources. It then employs the collected information to create an approximation through rational function interpolation, initially using the eigenvalues and subsequently the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the related linear equation. The process can be further enhanced by applying nonlinear transformations to both the problem and the approximating function for improved results. Two cases are examined to illustrate the performance of this method in practice.

We demonstrate the topological equivalence of all intermediate beta-transformations with a specific type of greedy beta-transformation that incorporates a hole at zero. This equivalence enables the natural extension of key properties and techniques, such as Hausdorff dimension calculations and asymptotic behavior of orbit hits, from existing studies on finite holes to new cases at the 0-hole endpoint. Consequently, we establish the linear growth, with a specific hit-asymptotic, of the return numbers to the 0-hole for all intermediate beta-transformations. Additionally, we derive the exact value of the Hausdorff dimension of the 0-hole for specific values of base and interval.

We've found that gauge theories with $SO(N_{c})$ as a gauge group and matter fields represented as vectors confine, resulting from monopole condensation and the quark bilinear breaking $SU(N_{F})$ chiral symmetry down to $SO(N_{F})$. Our findings derive from an ${\cal N}=1$ supersymmetric theory, specifically with anomaly-mediated supersymmetry breaking.

Machine learning models have high accuracy, but their complexity makes it difficult to understand their predictions. Tree-based ensembles, a popular class of models, pose additional interpretation challenges. We address these challenges by developing a new method called Disentangled Attribution Curves (DAC), which not only reveals important features but also their non-linear relationships with target outcomes. Compared to existing explanation methods, our approach offers higher accuracy and a more precise understanding of how features impact the target, as demonstrated in our experiments on synthetic and real datasets.

Federated learning offers a way to train machine learning models without compromising user privacy. However, this approach has a weakness where an adversary controlling the server can manipulate or steal model updates. Although existing solutions try to address this limitation, they either compromise model confidentiality or can't stop the adversary from modifying the updates. In this research, we introduce a novel method called TEEdrn that utilizes a Trusted Execution Environment to stop the adversary from modifying or stealing model updates. Additionally, we propose an efficient execution algorithm to maintain computation efficiency. Furthermore, we develop execution optimizations and execute them on Intel SGX, which gives us the first practical implementation of federated learning with both updated and model confidentiality secured. Experimental results show that our method scales efficiently and has only a 2.76x overhead in terms of training time.

The embedded systems industry is massive and ubiquitous, as evidenced by its presence in every electronic device we use. However, the most significant challenge lies in the external peripherals that embedded software interacts with, leading to well-known issues in embedded software development and testing. Although some testing tools have been created in an attempt to test embedded software, the most challenging aspect remains testing the interaction between the software and the hardware. Although Model-Based Design (MBD) has proven effective in controlling embedded systems, testing their dynamic behavior based on digital models has remained a challenging task. In this research, we present a method to test the dynamic behavior of controlled MBD-based embedded systems using formal verification. We represent the digital MBD models as finite-state machines (FSMs) using an extended version of Synchronous Data Flow (SDF) models, which includes models of external peripherals. We then convert the SF models into a format suitable for verification, using an extensible graph representation format called IR.

This paper introduces a new method called Timeloops, which dynamically identifies and removes unnecessary system calls not utilized by a given application, in contrast to static analysis techniques that may produce overly broad results. Focusing on containerized microservices, Timeloops utilizes a highly efficient and effective dynamic analysis technique called feedback-directed virtual execution, often referred to as an "oracle" approach. By analyzing an application's behavior, Timeloops generates a customized filter for system calls, reducing the number of actual system calls made and thereby decreasing the attack surface and the application's footprint. Additionally, Timeloops can be used to create a lightweight container with only necessary code sections, further shrinking the attack surface. Extensive testing using a service-oriented architecture framework and a web application revealed that Timeloops achieves filtering accuracy as high as 98.6% while significantly outperforming previous methods in accuracy and efficiency.

Advanced techniques for representing complex data rely on the ability to compress complex functions into simpler, yet still accurate, approximations. Previous studies have effectively demonstrated that certain types of classifiers can achieve precise approximation in both metric and Riemannian product spaces. Nonetheless, for linear classifiers of any metric or Riemannian product space, a significant question remained unresolved - whether these classifiers possess a universal ability to capture the structure of any product space through approximation. This limitation ultimately hinders learning linear relationships within metric or Riemannian product spaces. In this research, we resolve this outstanding problem by proving that, regardless of the curvature, the set of functions classifiable by linear classifiers in any product space can be precisely approximated by classifiers from a simplified version of the original space - one with only two dimensions. This universal ability to capture the structure of any metric or Riemannian product space opens up promising opportunities for learning within these complex spaces.

This introduction focuses on stochastic Model Predictive Control methods that account for uncertainty in constraints, illustrated through a linear system under unpredictable conditions. The corresponding Matlab code is also accessible online for reference purposes.

This paper bridges the gap between compressed sensing and statistical learning, focusing on compressive representation learning to minimize computational complexity in learning tasks. To achieve this, the paper leverages sparsity structure within datasets to compress data in an optimal manner, ensuring that information-rich directions are prioritized in data compression, while still enabling accurate training. Comprehensive experiments on various datasets are conducted to validate the proposed methods and demonstrate their efficacy.
